newsitem.title: EGYPT: Medinet Nasr turnover powers Cairo bourse.
newsitem.headline: Medinet Nasr turnover powers Cairo bourse.

text.p: Medinet Nasr Housing and Development powered turnover on Cairo's stock market on Tuesday and the index closed 1996 at its highest level in December.

The realty firm, the biggest gainer for the past two days, Tuesday boosted by 13.7 million pounds the day's total market turnover of 61.28 million pounds ($18.02 million). The share closed unchanged at 383.00 pounds.
Stock exchange officials had imposed a ceiling on the share because it felt brokers were overpricing the stock.
"The people who sold were those at the initial public offering so they are realising some profits before the year-end," Sherif Cararah of EFG/Hermes brokerage said of Medinet Nasr.
Bourse officials have frozen the price of another realty firm, Heliopolis Housing and Development.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index rose 4.83 points to 296.68 but pre-new year trade was generally subdued after many companies started paying out dividends.
"More or less people are quiet today but we expect for the market to jump in the first quarter," said Cararah. "Most of the stocks are affected by the coupon collections."
Amriyah Cement was the second most active stock. It closed down 2.00 pounds at 64.00 in 9.8 million pounds turnover.
It was the second day of the state's Holding Company for Metallurgical Industries' sale of about 3.4 million shares of the cement firm, or 17 percent of its equity.
United Arab Spinning and Weaving/Unirab shares were among the bourse's star performers when they gained 24.58 pounds to close at 78.00.
The Egyptian government said on Tuesday that it would offer investors a minimum 10 percent or 570,400 shares in partially privatised Unirab for two days from January 8, 1997.
Mills were relatively quiet, Cararah said, but they retained their status among the market's top ten most active shares.
The biggest gainer and most active of the milling shares was Central and West Delta Flour Mills, which ended up 4.25 pounds at 83.00 in turnover of 3.4 million.
The CMA index for openly traded firms fell to 440.76 points from 459.55 points on Monday while the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 205.04 from 204.75.
